| style="text-align:left; width:100%;" | <big>'''Foe changes:'''</big> As soon as you complete the first quest, [[spawn]]s of some areas in Cantha will change to fit the new story:
# These updated areas are more challenging than their ''Factions'' counterparts.
# These new spawns will be present even if other characters in the party have not completed ''Factions'' yet.
# To restore the default spawns, take [[Memories of Purity]] from the [[Herald of Purity]] in [[Kaineng Center]] (requires completion of [[Cleansing Morostav Trail]]).
|}

* To begin the story, speak with [[Initiate Zei Ri]], who can be found on the lower level of [[Kaineng Center]]. 
* The first twelve quests in the storyline consist of the [[Ministry of Purity]] sending you to cleanse areas of the [[Afflicted]].
* The next five quests involve fighting [[Am Fah]] and [[Jade Brotherhood]] on behalf of the ministry.
* The story jumps in a new direction, with seven quests that have you defending various unaligned groups across [[Cantha]].
* The next four quests involve defending the [[Angchu]] from various threats in [[Kaineng City]] and [[Shing Jea Island]].
* The next six quests involve defending Cantha from various threats in [[Kaineng City]] and [[Shing Jea Island]].
* You confront the end-storyline boss in the final quest.

=== Preparation ===

In order to progress through the full main storyline, you must have access to the following [[explorable area]]s:
* All zones on Shing Jea Island (requires [[Minister Cho's Estate]] and [[Zen Daijun]]).
* [[Rhea's Crater]] and [[Silent Surf]] (requires [[Gyala Hatchery]] ''or'' access to [[Unwaking Waters (Luxon)|the Luxon outpost for Unwaking Waters]]).
* [[Morostav Trail]] and [[Mourning Veil Falls]] (requires [[The Eternal Grove]] ''or'' access to [[Unwaking Waters (Kurzick)|the Kurzick outpost for Unwaking Waters]]).

=== General suggestions ===
{{see|Soul Explosion}}
* [[Martial]] professions will suffer if they choose to remain within [[melee range]] of ''[[Afflicted]]'' foes.
** Be prepared to deal with [[List of enchantment removal skills|enchantment removal skills]] often deployed by foes (such as [[Dark Soul Explosion]]); non-Dervish party members should avoid using enchantments.
** Although there are plenty of [[corpse]]s, many of the Necromancers carry [[:Category:Skills that target minions|minion stealing skill]]s; bring [[anti-summon skill]]s and use caution bringing [[minion master]]s.
** Exercise proper [[:Category:PvE tactics|PvE tactics]] at all times. Be careful not to over-[[aggro]]: plenty of groups overlap with [[patrol]] paths. 

; Threat assessment
* Target [[Afflicted Necromancer]]s and [[Afflicted Monk]]s early: they heal and dish out considerable area of effect (AoE) damage.
* Target [[Afflicted Ranger]]s and [[Afflicted Ritualist]]s last: their deaths can destroy all of your [[summoned creature]]s.
* Target [[Jade Brotherhood Warrior]]s early: their area of effect (AoE) damage can decimate your party.
* Target [[Sensali Mesmer]]s early: their area of effect (AoE) interrupts can shutdown all of your allies.

; Recommended skills
* Winds of Change foes are easy to ball up: bring [[area of effect]] (AoE) skills, including [[Panic]] and [[Ray of Judgment]].
* Winds of Change allied NPCs frequently appear: bring area of effect (AoE) protection and healing skills (so that your [[List of skills which affects allies|allies benefit]]), including [[Shelter]] and [[Union]].
* Winds of Change objectives can require protection of allies: bringing [[Blood is Power]] or minions allows you to exploit NPC's [[AI]], thereby allowing them to be lead to safety.
* Winds of Change features numerous hostile spirits and minions: bring [[anti-summon]] skills to help take them down quickly, including [[Spiritual Pain]] and [[Consume Soul]].
